narrative.overview: Hisab turns a bank receipt into an ongoing, authenticated financial record: the dense receipt ledger and the selected record’s human purpose stay visible together. The interface feels calm, exact, and private—closer to a well-kept account book than a promotional fintech dashboard. It deliberately avoids a generic grid of metric cards. The system combines mineral-paper surfaces, petrol ink, thin ruled dividers, restrained turquoise actions, small saffron signals, and condensed financial figures. Density is intentional: desktop preserves a scan-efficient operating surface, while smaller layouts progressively remove secondary metadata and recast rows for touch without losing the receipt-and-purpose relationship. The product truth is specific: the source image is processed locally in the browser and is never uploaded; only user-reviewed fields and extracted OCR text are persisted to the signed-in user’s private D1 records.
keyCharacteristics: Authenticated receipt ledger with records scoped to the signed-in user.
Local-image OCR followed by required human review before persistence.
Receipt-led split view with a dense ledger and contextual inspector.
Deep-ink navigation rail and pale, low-chroma working surfaces.
Turquoise reserved for actions, selection, connectivity, and trustworthy emphasis.
Condensed numerals for balances and amounts; humanist sans-serif for working text.
Ruled lines, dashed receipt separators, and tonal fills provide most structure.

rules.name: The Action-Only Turquoise Rule
rules.body: Turquoise signals an available action, active selection, or confirmed connection; it is not decorative background color.

rules.name: The Saffron Restraint Rule
rules.body: Saffron is reserved for exceptional attention and never competes with receipt content.

rules.name: The Financial Figure Rule
rules.body: Use Roboto Condensed for balances and transaction amounts, not prose or navigation.

rules.name: The Dense-but-Legible Rule
rules.body: Small metadata is supported by strong contrast, short phrases, generous row height, and clear grouping; do not shrink primary actions or merchant names to metadata scale.

rules.name: The Paper-First Depth Rule
rules.body: Prefer borders, paper tones, and selection fills before adding a shadow.

dos: Do keep the ledger and selected receipt visually connected on wide screens.
Do reserve Roboto Condensed for balances and transaction amounts.
Do use thin solid rules for interface structure and dashed rules for receipt/accounting semantics.
Do preserve keyboard focus outlines, readable contrast, text status labels, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do simplify secondary metadata responsively while preserving merchant, amount, date, and note context.
Do distinguish local image handling from persisted receipt data: say the image is never uploaded, while confirmed fields and extracted OCR text are saved to the private account.
Do keep OCR, review, saving, and persistence-failure states visually and verbally distinct.
Do return focus to the opening control after modal cancellation and prevent cancellation while a save is in flight.
donts: Don't replace the operating surface with a generic grid of detached metric cards.
Don't use turquoise as a decorative wash across large regions; its rarity carries interaction meaning.
Don't round the signature receipt into an ordinary card or remove its dashed and scalloped paper cues.
Don't introduce heavy shadows on routine controls and cards.
Don't imply money movement, live-bank certification, or production connectivity through visual language or copy.
Don't claim that nothing leaves the device: reviewed fields and OCR text are intentionally persisted, while only the source image remains local.
Don't bypass review or save automatically after OCR, even when receiver and amount extraction appears confident.
